correctness.rationale: The identity exp(2πif_μ(s))=(z−μ)/(z(1−μz)) converts antipodal two-cycle condition into z^5−μz^4+μz−1=(z−1)(z⁴+(1−μ)(z³+z²+z)+1). The reciprocal quartic gives w²+(1−μ)w−(1+μ)=0, two w roots in (−2,2), hence four antipodal nonfixed points. All DT have positive entries and determinant one, so every fixed point of T² is nondegenerate (positive 2×2 determinant-one matrices have trace>2). Compact continuation from cat map count |det(A²−I)|=5 and unique fixed point proves two-cycle exhaustiveness. The +/- orbit derivatives agree and their exact Poisson kernels give the stated arcosh exponents, separation, linear μ onset and distinct square-root μ→1 laws. Direct torus double iteration and full Jacobian eigenvalue checks were performed for five μ; they are corroborative, not the global proof.
